correctness.rationale: The phase marginal is Haar because the lifted phase rotates at constant nonzero speed. Arbitrary antiderivative tests in x and y give the two conditional laws. The mechanical energy balance and phase uniformity yield the RMS inequality by Cauchy–Schwarz. The zero endpoint is impossible under nonzero forcing, while equality at the upper endpoint would force a sinusoidal velocity whose induced position makes the Duffing equation a cubic polynomial identity with nonzero cubic coefficient, a contradiction. The cubic barycenter identity gives the one-well sign-change theorem. All algebraic steps and the equality-obstruction coefficient were replayed in the packaged checker.

value.rationale: Mean-square velocity is the dissipative activity in the canonical forced Duffing oscillator, so a parameter-only ceiling in terms of forcing amplitude and damping is physically intrinsic. The strictness is substantive: the cubic nonlinearity rules out the only equality profile allowed by the power estimate. The exact nonlinear-load regression provides an attractor-independent calibration for simulations and reduced statistical models, while the one-well theorem forces recurrent trajectories to straddle the unforced potential minimum rather than remaining on one side of it. These are structural constraints on periodic and chaotic stationary states, not merely numerical characteristics of one parameter set.
